Gold approaches $4,170, silver gains 3% as bond rally lifts precious metals - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Gold and silver prices are sharply higher in late U.S. trading Thursday, as falling Treasury yields, a weaker U.S. dollar and renewed safe-haven demand helped precious metals recover from Wednesday's inflation-driven selloff. A stronger-than-expected U.S. producer inflation report failed to reverse the rally in government bonds , with concerns over heavily indebted artificial intelligence companies drawing capital into Treasuries. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,168.70 an ounce, up $64.20, or 1.56%, while spot silver was trading near $57.310, up $1.800, or 3.24%. North American equities closed higher after recovering from sharp early losses, as falling Treasury yields and strength outside the technology sector offset continuing concerns about AI infrastructure spending. The S&P 500 advanced 0.3%, recovering from an early decline of approximately 0.6%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1.1%, supported by health care, retail and other defensive shares. The Nasdaq Composite finished 0.1% higher after reversing an intraday loss of approximately 1.4%. Technology shares remained volatile, but broader market participation improved as the session progressed. European equities also finished mostly higher, with earnings strength and defensive-sector demand helping the region outperform technology-heavy markets in Asia. The Stoxx Europe 600 gained approximately 0.3% to 639.85. The U.K. FTSE 100 rose 1.08% to 10,840.35, Germany's DAX added 0.33% to 25,382.62 and France's CAC 40 climbed 0.78% to 7,934.70. Italy's FTSE MIB bucked the broader advance, declining 0.72% to 49,397.55. European health care and telecommunications shares outperformed, while technology and banking stocks faced selling pressure.

items.titleEn: China buys the gold dip as ETF holdings hit record and holiday demand lifts Q4 outlook – WGC
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – China’s central bank added 23 tonnes of gold to its reserves last month, while the country’s gold ETFs saw healthy inflows in September to cap a strong quarter, and the recent holidays and festivals saw demand for gold jewelry, bars and coins rise as prices moderated, according to Ray Jia, research head for China at the World Gold Council (WGC). In the WGC’s latest China gold market update, Jia noted that while gold’s September price declines cut into Q3 gains, the yellow metal still advanced during the quarter. “Gold pulled back in September (Chart 1), with the LBMA Gold Price PM in USD and the SHAUPM in RMB falling 8.5% and 5.5%, respectively,” he said. “According to our gold return attribution model (GRAM), soaring US Treasury yields amid the Fed’s tightening moves and the strengthening dollar weighed on gold.”

items.titleEn: Bitcoin is starting to behave more like gold as investors seek alternative hedges – Block Scholes
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold has managed to push back above $4,100 an ounce, but the precious metal continues to face significant headwinds from persistent inflation fears, which are driving hawkish monetary policies around the world. However, gold is not the only alternative asset attracting attention as investors look to protect their wealth against currency debasement and broader financial market risks. According to one market analyst, Bitcoin is increasingly behaving like gold, suggesting that investors could be starting to view the digital currency as a supplementary safe-haven asset rather than simply another speculative risk asset. In a note published Thursday, Thahbib Rahman, Research Analyst at Block Scholes, said that Bitcoin's correlation with gold is at its highest level since November 2020, when pandemic-era fiscal and monetary stimulus gripped financial markets.

items.titleEn: Amazon and Walmart Are Turning Retail Efficiency Into Someone Else's Expense
items.summaryEn: Retail automation may shift costs rather than eliminate them. Walmart’s robotics investments could improve fulfillment economics while requiring suppliers to spend more on packaging, infrastructure and working capital. Amazon is moving upstream of the shopping search. Its new Bee integrations turn conversation-derived reminders into product recommendations, potentially increasing platform influence over consumer demand. The next retail margin battle is about who captures the savings. As platforms control more of discovery and fulfillment, CFOs must evaluate innovation across the entire transaction rather than isolated productivity gains.
